title: fullcycle --dry-run prints a weaker command than it runs, because the clean flags are decided in two places
body:
## Summary

`fullcycle --dry-run` prints a command line that is not the one `fullcycle` runs, and omits the only line that says a consent is being given on the operator's behalf.

Measured 2026-09-02 on a fixture estate:

    $ bin/devbin fullcycle --dry-run
          bin/devbin clean rust
          bin/devbin build all
          bin/devbin test rust

The real run executes `bin/devbin clean rust --force-blocked`. `_fullcycle_run` appends `--force-blocked` unconditionally and the `clean*` arm of the phase loop passes it; the preview re-derives the flag list separately and still carries only the pre-0047 rule.

## Two homes for one decision, and they already disagree

The flags are decided twice:

- `_fullcycle_run`: `pass+=(--force-blocked)` then `[ "$force" = 1 ] && pass+=(--force)`
- `cmd_fullcycle`'s dry branch: `case "$phase" in clean*) [ "$force" = 1 ] && printf ' --force' ;; esac`

Issue `0047` changed the first on 2026-09-02 and did not touch the second, which is exactly what a duplicated decision does when only one copy is maintained. **The two were in agreement before 0047, so nothing in the 0047 diff looked wrong.**

## The part that is not cosmetic

A real run prints, when `--force` was not given:

      - fullcycle HAS answered clean's blocked-binaries refusal for you, ...
      - it has NOT answered the removal prompt. ...

The dry branch returns before `_fullcycle_run` is reached, so **the preview prints none of it.** An operator using `--dry-run` to decide whether to run the thing sees neither the flag nor the sentence explaining what the flag concedes. The preview is the surface most likely to be read by someone who has not read the code, and it is the one that omits the concession.

## Why a dry run getting this wrong is its own category

A `--dry-run` has exactly one contract: the command it describes is the command it would run. This one describes a strictly weaker invocation than it executes -- the previewed form would REFUSE on a blocked tree where the real form proceeds. A reader checking the preview to satisfy themselves about safety is reading a safer command than the one that will run.

## Fix direction

One home for the flag list, read by both paths, and the no---force notice printed by the dry run as well as by the real one.

The existing test `--dry-run reflects whether --force was given` cannot catch this: it asserts `refute_output_contains "clean rust --force"`, and `--force-blocked` satisfies that containment as a prefix. **The assertion is a prefix of the string it means to forbid**, which is the same over-wide-assertion class already on this project's record.
